scope: Compatibility of declared runtime values and dependency graphs. This does not prove a foreign implementation obeys its declared contract or provide machine ABI adapters.
rules: The default VerifiedIR validator rejects external imports without an explicit interface context.
An explicit context has unique module identities, valid closed exports, resolved public shapes, a supported semantic/value profile, target availability and allowed capability requirements.
Imports bind the exact selected module and exported name; function and value types must match.
Every named type reachable from an import has identical public field/constructor order, names, types and generic binders in provider and consumer, including recursive layouts.
Linked-module exports are derived from actual declarations and every body is independently revalidated; callers cannot substitute an asserted export signature for a body.
All imports resolve within the complete graph or explicit host contracts. Private exports, duplicate module identities and dependency cycles reject.
A module declares at least the capabilities required by each dependency, so capabilities cannot disappear through transitive links.
The result retains selected interfaces, target policy and a deterministic dependency order. Host contracts retain explicit assumption identities.
Validation depth exhaustion rejects; it never changes an unknown result into acceptance.
supportedRepresentation: The existing target-neutral VerifiedIR types: primitive values, owned functions, Array, named records and variants. Representation equality is nominal and exact; no structural cast, foreign pointer, borrowed lifetime or erased type is inferred.
unsupported: polymorphic exported declarations at the external module boundary
foreign resource/handle ownership and destruction protocols
borrowed values, async streams and futures
automatic WIT, native ABI or foreign calling-convention conversion
remaining: target-specific adapter implementation and independent validation
artifact/evidence binding of each dependency interface and resulting linked artifacts
global semantic link preservation and validator soundness
